title: Virginia Sales Tax Guide: Rates, Compliance, and Regulations for Businesses
summary: A complete guide to Virginia's sales tax rates, regulations, and everything else businesses need to know to stay compliant.
body_markdown:
## Virginia sales tax at a glance


State taxing authority Virginia Department of Taxation


Virginia sales tax rate 4.3% state rate plus a mandatory 1% local rate (5.3% combined minimum)


Regional and local tax rates 0% to 1.7% on top of the 5.3% base rate, depending on location


Combined sales tax rate range 5.3% to 7%


Economic nexus threshold $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 transactions


Website[tax.virginia.gov](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/)


Tax line(804) 367-8037


Most of Virginia has a 5.3% combined sales tax rate, made up of a 4.3% state tax plus a 1% local tax. Add a 0.7% regional transportation tax in Northern Virginia, Hampton Roads, and Central Virginia, and the rate goes to 6%.


In Danville and seven Southside and Eastern Shore localities, it's 6.3%. In the Historic Triangle, made up of Williamsburg, James City County, and York County, it’s 7%.


Tangible personal property is taxable across the board, though groceries and certain hygiene products only pay the reduced 1% rate rather than sitting exempt.


[Economic nexus in Virginia](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/virginia) kicks in once a business hits $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 transactions into the state in the current or prior year, whether they have a physical presence or not.


Numeral's[free nexus monitoring](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) can warn you when you are nearing and reaching the threshold.


Virginia, not the business, decides whether filing is monthly or quarterly, based on tax liability.


SaaS and electronically delivered software are generally not taxable in Virginia, a stance fewer than half of states share. Marketplace-only sellers usually do not need their own registration, since the facilitator handles collection.

## Virginia sales tax rates and calculations


Depending on where the sale is delivered, Virginia's combined rate lands anywhere from 5.3% to 7%.


The gap comes from regional transportation taxes and the Historic Triangle's added local levy, not from a patchwork of city-by-city rates the way many states structure local tax.


### Special Virginia sales tax rates


[Virginia's rate structure](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/retail-sales-and-use-tax) sorts into four tiers:


Combined Rate Where It Applies


**5.3%** Most of the state (4.3% state tax plus the mandatory 1% local tax)


**6%** Northern Virginia, Hampton Roads and Central Virginia (adds a 0.7% regional transportation tax)


**6.3%** Charlotte County, Danville, Gloucester County, Halifax County, Henry County, Northampton County, Patrick County and Pittsylvania County


**7%** Historic Triangle: Williamsburg, James City County and York County (adds a 1% regional tax)


Because regional and local boundaries don't always follow zip codes or city lines, the exact rate can shift depending on the specific address. Use Virginia's official[Sales Tax Rate and Locality Code Lookup](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sales-tax-rate-and-locality-code-lookup) before applying a rate to a sale.


### How to calculate Virginia sales tax


Multiply the taxable sale amount by the combined rate for the delivery address. A $100 taxable purchase carries $5.30 in tax at the 5.3% base rate, or $7 at the Historic Triangle's 7% rate. Groceries and qualifying hygiene products use the flat 1% rate instead, regardless of location.


### Origin- vs. destination-based sourcing in Virginia


Virginia taxes are destination-based, meaning they depend on where the buyer receives the product, not where the seller is based. This determines which of the four rate tiers applies to a given sale. A business shipping to the Historic Triangle collects 7%, even if it's located in a 5.3% area.


### Is Virginia a Streamlined Sales Tax State?


No. Virginia isn't part of the[Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/) , which means it won't accept the SST exemption certificate or SST's multistate registration. Businesses use Virginia's own forms for registration and resale exemptions instead.


## Sales tax nexus in Virginia


Nexus is the connection between a business and a state that creates a duty to collect that state's sales tax.


Before the[2018 Wayfair Supreme Court decision](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , states could only require businesses with a physical presence to collect. That ruling let states, Virginia included, base the requirement on sales volume alone, effective July 1, 2019.


Virginia recognizes physical, economic, marketplace, and affiliate nexus, though physical and economic nexus matter most for typical businesses.


Nexus Type Threshold


**Physical**[Physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) is established by any physical presence in Virginia, including an office, warehouse, employees, or stored inventory.


**Economic**[Virginia’s economic nexus threshold](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/virginia) is $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 separate transactions into Virginia during the current or prior calendar year.


**Marketplace**[Marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) exceeding Virginia’s economic nexus threshold must collect and remit sales tax on behalf of their sellers.


**Affiliate** A rebuttable presumption of nexus applies when a commonly controlled business helps establish or maintain a market in Virginia, such as through a shared warehouse.


### Economic nexus for remote sellers explained


Since July 1, 2019, Virginia has enforced[economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) . If a remote seller's gross revenue tops $100,000, or it makes 200 or more separate retail sale transactions into the state in the current or prior calendar year, that seller has crossed the threshold.


The dollar threshold counts gross revenue, not just taxable revenue, so exempt sales still contribute toward it. A seller that stops meeting both thresholds for a full calendar year can drop its collection obligation the following January.


### Marketplace sellers and facilitators


A seller whose Virginia sales go through a[marketplace facilitator](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) generally does not need its own registration, since the facilitator already collects the tax.


If that seller also makes direct sales, such as through its own website, only those direct sales count against the $100,000 or 200-transaction threshold. Marketplace facilitators themselves must register once their combined direct and facilitated sales cross the same threshold.


## What's taxable and exempt in Virginia


Virginia taxes most retail sales of tangible personal property, along with a short list of specific services.[Digital goods](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) and[SaaS fall outside the VA tax base](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-virginia) entirely, a narrower approach than most states take.


Category Taxable? Notes


**Tangible personal property** Yes Most physical goods are taxable unless specifically exempt


**Groceries** Reduced rate Taxed at a flat 1% local rate instead of the combined rate


**Clothing** Yes No general clothing exemption


**Prescription drugs** No Exempt statewide


**SaaS** No Treated as a nontaxable service


**Digital goods** No Downloaded or streamed products are generally exempt when no tangible medium is provided


**Services** Varies Most professional and personal services are exempt unless tied to a taxable sale


**Shipping** Varies Exempt if separately stated and not combined with handling


### What is subject to sales tax in Virginia


- Most tangible personal property, from furniture to electronics
- Prewritten software delivered on a physical disc or drive
- Meals and prepared food sold by restaurants and caterers
- Accommodations, including hotel and short-term rental stays
- Certain repair, maintenance, and fabrication services tied to a taxable sale
- Communications services, taxed separately under Virginia's communications sales tax


### What's exempt from sales tax in Virginia


- Prescription drugs and certain medical devices
- Most professional services, including legal, accounting and consulting work
- Sales for resale, when backed by a valid exemption certificate
- Certain agricultural supplies and equipment used in farming
- Textbooks required for courses at accredited Virginia schools


### Groceries get a reduced rate, not an exemption


Groceries, meaning food for home consumption, and certain essential hygiene products aren't exempt in Virginia. They're taxed at a flat 1% statewide. The state dropped its own portion of the[grocery tax](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/grocery-tax) on Jan. 1, 2023, leaving only the 1% local tax in place.


The 1% rate holds everywhere, even in the 6%, 6.3%, and 7% regions, but it doesn't cover prepared or hot food meant for immediate consumption.


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in Virginia


Virginia has long treated prewritten software delivered entirely electronically, with no tangible medium provided, as a nontaxable transaction.[Cloud computing and SaaS are generally not taxable in VA](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-virginia) since no physical property changes hands.


Software delivered on a disc or drive, or bundled with hardware, remains taxable.


The same logic extends to digital products like downloaded music, movies, and e-books, which are generally not taxable when delivered electronically.


Lawmakers have proposed bills that would extend the sales tax to digital services and digital personal property, so this treatment could change in a future legislative session.


### Resale and exemption certificates in Virginia


Businesses buying goods for resale use[Form ST-10](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/taxforms/exemption-certificates/any/st-10-any.pdf) , the Sales and Use Tax Certificate of Exemption. The buyer needs an active Virginia sales tax registration and must include that account number on the certificate.


Virginia is not among the states listed on the[Multistate Tax Commission](https://www.mtc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Unif-Resale-Cert-revised-10-14-22.pdf) Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate. They are also not a member state of[the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/home) .


[You can use out-of-state resale certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/states-that-dont-accept-out-of-state-resale-certificates) only if they include the same information the ST-10 requires and a Virginia registration number.


Certificates have no fixed expiration date, but sellers should keep them for at least three years, in line with the general sales tax recordkeeping rule.


## Registering for a Virginia sales tax license


Virginia calls its sales tax registration a Certificate of Registration. Most businesses register online through[Virginia Tax’s business online services](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/register-business-virginia) . If you're unable to register online, you can fill out and mail[Form R-1](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/taxforms/business-registration/any/r-1-any.pdf) instead. There is no fee to register.


To register, a business needs:


- Business information (legal name, business address, mailing address, entity type)
- Your business’s Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN)
- Start date of business activity in Virginia
- Contact information for your business
- Responsible party information, if applicable (name, Social Security number, address, contact information)
- Your[North American Industry Classification System](https://www.census.gov/naics/) (NAICS) code


Once Virginia approves the application, it assigns a sales tax account number and mails a Certificate of Registration, which you must post somewhere visible at the registered location.


Your Certificate of Registration doesn't expire, and you don't have to renew it. It stays valid as long as your business is active and your sales tax account is open. If you close the business, sell it, or change its ownership, notify Virginia Tax so it can close or update your account.


### Registration requirements for remote sellers


Out-of-state dealers register the same way in-state dealers do, using the online portal or the Form R-1. Once a seller passes $100,000 or reaches 200 transactions in the current or prior calendar year, it has 30 days from the day it establishes nexus to register and start collecting.


Since Virginia is not a Streamlined member, remote sellers cannot use SST's single multistate registration to cover Virginia alongside other states.


## Collecting Virginia sales tax


Once registered, a business needs to determine whether a sale is taxable, apply the correct rate for the delivery address, collect the tax at checkout, and track what it collects for reporting. Most sales use one of the four combined rate tiers; groceries and qualifying hygiene products use the flat 1% rate instead.


### Marketplace sales


When a sale runs through a[marketplace facilitator](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) like Amazon, Etsy, or Walmart Marketplace, that facilitator collects and remits Virginia sales tax. Sellers don't have to collect tax separately on those sales, though they should keep tracking them for nexus purposes.


Sellers must also maintain their registration and collect tax on any direct sales made outside the marketplace.


### Shipping and delivery charges


Separately stated[shipping and delivery charges](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) are exempt from Virginia sales tax, but handling charges are taxable. If shipping and handling are billed as one combined charge, even one labeled "shipping and handling," the entire charge becomes taxable.


To keep delivery charges exempt, sellers must list them separately from any handling fee on the invoice.


## Filing and paying Virginia sales tax


Virginia assigns a monthly or quarterly filing frequency based on tax liability and periodically reviews that assignment.


Even with nothing owed, returns are due on the 20th of the month after the filing period closes, and businesses must file and pay electronically through[Virginia Tax's online services](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/retail-sales-and-use-tax) for businesses.


### Filing Virginia sales tax online


[Businesses file and pay through Virginia Tax's online services](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-virginia-sales-tax-online) for businesses, which also handles registration updates and account management. Businesses with an average monthly liability above $20,000 must pay by[electronic funds transfer](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/business-tax-payment-options) .


Virginia has no separate local filing system, since it collects regional and local rates with the state rate on one return.


## Virginia sales tax penalties and interest


[A late return](https://www.numeral.com/blog/what-happens-if-you-dont-collect-or-remit-sales-tax) costs 6% per month or partial month, up to a cap of 30% of the tax due, and there's a $10 minimum penalty even if no tax was owed.


On top of that, unpaid tax accrues interest at the federal underpayment rate plus 2% until it's settled.


## Virginia sales tax recordkeeping and audits


Sales records, exemption and resale certificates, and returns and payment records must be kept for at least three years, counted from the return's due date or filing date, whichever comes later.


That's the window the Department of Taxation can[audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) within, checking reported sales, taxability decisions, exemptions claimed, rates applied, and whether the right amount actually got collected and remitted.


Businesses that disagree with an audit finding can appeal through the Department of Taxation’s[administrative appeals process](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/administrative-appeals) , with further review available in court. Details are available through Virginia Tax's official guidance.

## Virginia sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in Virginia?** Depending on location, rates run from 5.3% up to 7%. Most of the state pays 5.3%, split between a 4.3% state tax and a 1% mandatory local tax.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in Virginia?** $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 separate transactions delivered into the state, in the current or prior calendar year. Either threshold alone triggers the registration requirement.


**Are services taxable in Virginia?** Only a short list of enumerated services is taxable, mainly those tied to a taxable sale of tangible property. Most professional and personal services, including legal, accounting, and consulting work, are exempt.


**Is SaaS taxable in Virginia?** No. Virginia treats SaaS as a nontaxable service, since no tangible property changes hands.


**Are digital products taxable in Virginia?** Generally not. Digital products delivered electronically, like downloaded music or e-books, are not taxable unless bundled with a taxable tangible item.


**Does Virginia charge sales tax on shipping and delivery?** Only if it is billed as combined "shipping and handling" or bundled with a handling fee. A separately stated shipping charge alone is exempt.


**Do I need a sales tax permit in Virginia?** Yes, once you have physical or economic nexus in the state. Businesses register through[Virginia Tax’s business online services](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/register-business-virginia) or by mail using Form R-1.


**Do marketplace sellers need to collect sales tax in Virginia?** Not on marketplace sales, since facilitators collect and remit that tax. Sellers still need to register and collect tax on any direct sales made outside the marketplace.


**How often do businesses need to file sales tax returns in Virginia?** Virginia assigns each business a monthly or quarterly frequency based on tax liability. Returns are due on the 20th of the month following the filing period, even with no tax due.


**Are groceries and clothing taxable in Virginia?** Groceries are taxed at a reduced 1% rate rather than exempted outright. Clothing has no general exemption and is taxed at the full combined rate.
